entries.name: Howard Gresham Hawkins III

expected.charges: Criminal trespass (April 30 – May 1, 1977 mass occupation of the Seabrook Nuclear Power Plant construction site, NH)
expected.sentence: Held without bail in NH National Guard armory ~13 days; criminal trespass charges most dismissed.

updates.sentence: Arrested during the May 1, 1977 Seabrook occupation and released early because of a shortage of beds. The exact release day and duration of his detention have not been established.

entries.rationale: Own interview explicitly May Day arrest and early release, not13days. Mayrelease already month precision; preserve. No actualnumeric toclear in snapshot.

entries.name: George Young

expected.charges: Charged in connection with the death of Marian Pyszko, a white autoworker beaten to death by a crowd during the July 1975 Livernois–Fenkell rebellion in Detroit.
expected.sentence:
None — acquitted after roughly eleven months in custody awaiting and standing trial.

Verdict as recorded: No — held for about eleven months and tried three times; all five defendants were acquitted and released.

Charges as recorded: Charged in connection with the death of Marian Pyszko, a white autoworker beaten to death by a crowd during the July 1975 Livernois–Fenkell rebellion in Detroit — one of five young Black men rounded up in a police dragnet that critics condemned as a racist sweep of anyone who could be tied to the area, even as the white bar owner whose killing of Obie Wynn set off the rebellion faced only a misdemeanor.

updates.sentence: Charges dismissed before trial. Contemporary reporting distinguishes Young and Douglas Lane, who were freed earlier, from Peoples, Henderson and Jordan, who remained jailed through the third trial. Young's exact custody endpoints and actual duration remain unresolved.

entries.rationale: Primary February1976 Torch says Young charges dropped before case tried; June1976 thirdtrial onlyPeoples/Henderson/Jordan. Elevenmonthtotal wrongly generalized toYoung; clear, preserve1975yearstart.

entries.name: Stephen Donaldson

expected.charges: Arrest at 1973 Quaker peace protest at the White House; exact statutory charge unverified
expected.sentence: Jailed in Washington, D.C. after the 1973 peace protest. Beth Taylor’s account describes refusal to pay $10 and later release with help from the local Quaker meeting. No imposed prison term, exact arrest or release date, conviction for this protest, or total time served is established in the reviewed sources. Custody dates remain unset rather than assigning an invented day within 1973. Sexual assault in custody is documented by NYPL and his later advocacy organization. Later criminal custody is separate. Sources: https://archives.nypl.org/mss/824 ; https://cds.library.brown.edu/projects/WritingVietnam/bethspeech.html ; https://justdetention.org/who-we-are/our-history/

updates.sentence: Pretrial custody in District of Columbia Jail from August 14 through August 23, 1973 after the White House pray-in and refusal to post $10 bail. Released eight hours after Lucy Witt paid bail on August 23. Tried September 28 and acquitted October 1, 1973. This case excludes his separate overnight detention following the August 9 White House protest. No prison sentence imposed in this proceeding.

entries.rationale: Primary first-person account by Bob Martin (Donaldson legal name established by NYPL), Friends Journal October 1, 1974, printed pp487–488, explicitly verifies August14 detention and actual August23 release. Printed495 reports October1 acquittal. Original pp487–488 visually verified in agent-three-donaldson-07.png and -08.png. Existing case describes this $10-bail episode; earlier August9–10 overnight custody is distinct.
